title: Producers and Directors
description: Produce or direct stage, television, radio, video, or film productions for entertainment, information, or instruction. Responsible for creative decisions, such as interpretation of script, choice of actors or guests, set design, sound, special effects, and choreography.

tasks.text: Plan details such as framing, composition, camera movement, sound, and actor movement for each shot or scene.
Compose and edit scripts or provide screenwriters with story outlines from which scripts can be written.
Identify and approve equipment and elements required for productions, such as scenery, lights, props, costumes, choreography, and music.
Establish pace of programs and sequences of scenes according to time requirements and cast and set accessibility.
Cut and edit film or tape to integrate component parts into desired sequences.
Write and edit news stories from information collected by reporters and other sources.
Choose settings and locations for films and determine how scenes will be shot in these settings.
Supervise and coordinate the work of camera, lighting, design, and sound crew members.
Perform management activities, such as budgeting, scheduling, planning, and marketing.
Resolve personnel problems that arise during the production process by acting as liaisons between dissenting parties when necessary.
Coordinate the activities of writers, directors, managers, and other personnel throughout the production process.
Perform administrative duties, such as preparing operational reports, distributing rehearsal call sheets and script copies, and arranging for rehearsal quarters.
Arrange financing for productions.

clusters.label: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others

tasks.text: Communicate to actors the approach, characterization, and movement needed for each scene in such a way that rehearsals and takes are minimized.
Direct live broadcasts, films and recordings, or non-broadcast programming for public entertainment or education.
Review film, recordings, or rehearsals to ensure conformance to production and broadcast standards.
Review film daily to check on work in progress and to plan for future filming.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with technical directors, managers, crew members, and writers to discuss details of production, such as photography, script, music, sets, and costumes.
Conduct meetings with staff to discuss production progress and to ensure production objectives are attained.
Study and research scripts to determine how they should be directed.
Obtain rights to scripts or to such items as existing video footage.

clusters.label: Resolving Conflicts and Negotiating with Others

tasks.text: Negotiate with parties, including independent producers and the distributors and broadcasters who will be handling completed productions.
Hold auditions for parts or negotiate contracts with actors determined suitable for specific roles.
Research production topics using the internet, video archives, and other informational sources.
Write and submit proposals to bid on contracts for projects.
Consult with writers, producers, or actors about script changes or "workshop" scripts, through rehearsal with writers and actors to create final drafts.
Compile scripts, program notes, and other material related to productions.
Develop marketing plans for finished products, collaborating with sales associates to supervise product distribution.
Select plays, scripts, books, news content, or ideas to be produced.
Hire principal cast members and crew members, such as art directors, cinematographers, and costume designers.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Management of Financial Resources
skills.def: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Canva.

skills.name: Video creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to enable production of video content. Examples: Adobe After Effects, Adobe Premiere Pro, AP ENPS, Apple Final Cut Pro.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Google Workspace software, Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Cascading style sheets CSS, Drupal, Hypertext markup language HTML, JavaScript.
